Check out WizeFiles — a powerful, full-featured Android file manager. https://wizesoft.me/WizeFiles
Current answers for browsing, transfers, search, connectivity, security, backup, and privacy in WizeFiles.
What can I do with WizeFiles?

WizeFiles can browse local, root-capable, network, and cloud storage; copy, move, rename, share, and delete items; edit text; preview supported content; create and edit archives; and run longer jobs through Transfer Center.
Why does the app ask for file access?

WizeFiles needs storage access so it can display, copy, move, rename, and delete files that you choose to manage. Bluetooth, nearby-device, notification, biometric, and network permissions are requested only when a feature needs them.
How does the Trash Bin work?

When Trash Bin is enabled, supported deleted items are moved there first so you can restore them later. Emptying the bin, permanently deleting an item, or disabling the feature while it contains items cannot be undone.
Can I connect to network or cloud storage?

Yes. Add FTP, SFTP, SMB, WebDAV, or supported cloud providers such as Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, pCloud, MEGA, and S3-compatible storage. For OAuth providers, sign-in happens on the provider’s page.
Where can I track long file operations?

Open Tools > Transfer Center to follow copy, move, extraction, signing, and nearby-transfer jobs. Depending on the job state, you can pause, resume, retry failed work, reorder queued work, or open its destination.
How does Indexed instant search work?

Enable it in App Settings. WizeFiles builds and maintains an on-device index of local files so searches can return results without scanning storage every time. Tap Search index in Settings to inspect or rebuild it.

Open Tools > Sync & Backup to create reusable folder pairs and preview planned changes before starting. Review the selected mode and conflict rules in the preview so you know which side will be updated.

Open Tools > Nearby Transfer to copy files or complete folders directly between nearby WizeFiles devices. Bluetooth discovers and authenticates devices, Wi‑Fi carries the transfer, and a one-time QR code verifies the connection. Sending never deletes the originals.
How can I protect the file browser?
In App Settings > Security, create a password and enable Protect Browser. You can optionally offer biometric unlock first, keep password fallback, and choose how quickly WizeFiles locks again.
Can I back up App Settings?

Yes. Use App Settings > Backup & Restore to save supported preferences and optionally encrypt the backup. Storage accounts and the security password are intentionally excluded and must be configured again after restore.
How do bookmarks and pinned folders help?

Bookmarks save frequently used folders for quick access. Pinned default folders keep common locations visible in navigation, and Storage Locations controls which device, network, and cloud roots appear.
Can I change the app appearance?
Yes. App Settings includes Light, Dark, or System default themes, an optional pure-black dark theme, file icon shapes, list animations, and the long-file-name display style.
Does WizeFiles send crash reports or analytics automatically?

No. After a crash, a sanitized report is saved only on your device. You can review, copy, email, share, or discard it, and diagnostic logs are included only if you choose. Starting Email or Share marks that pending report as handled so WizeFiles does not ask again.
Does the FAQ or About section open the web?
The FAQ is built into the app and works offline. External pages such as the website, privacy policy, Play Store, or email app open only when you choose the related About action.
